Hiro,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Orchard is moving forward with a private VPC deployment for our analytics assistant and procurement wants a short sizing proposal so they can greenlight budgets and procurement lead times. High-level ask below — we can follow up with a call if helpful.

What we need from Redwood:
- Recommended baseline pool size (GPU count/type) to meet sustained throughput target and latency SLOs.
- Burst scaling strategy (how much headroom, autoscale timing, expected warm-up).
- Networking requirements (bandwidth per node, firewall/VPC rules, NFS vs local cache recommendations).
- Any expected procurement lead time / minimum order constraints you see for Dedicated-like deployments (we're buying through a cloud partner).

Orchard constraints/assumptions:
- Model: customer intends to run an Llama-2-chat-like 13B family (we're open to 8-bit quantized variants).
- Typical request: 1 short instruction + ~80 token prompt; expected response ~350 tokens.
- SLOs: 95% requests < 600ms token-latency (end-to-end target TBD), target p99 under heavy load is a follow-up ask.
- Expected steady-state: 60 requests/s; anticipated burst up to 120 requests/s for short windows (3–10 minutes) during batch analysis windows.

I've attached Orchard's infra profile (orchard_infra_profile.xlsx). Can you get us a short runbook and numbers we can put into procurement?

Hi all — below is a concise proposal / assumptions for Orchard's baseline and burst strategy. Attached: capacity_calc_20261120.xlsx (detailed calc) + a simple network diagram.

Assumptions (call out):
- Effective tokens per request = prompt (80) + response (350) + model overhead ~ 430 tokens.
- Average token generation time / model-profile: we measured an optimized 13B-quantized path to ~8–10 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent GPU when serving streaming chat with optimizations (kernel tiling, KV cache warm). We'll use a conservative estimate of 9 tokens/sec for perf planning.
- For latency SLO (~600ms per request), the driver is tail token generation. To meet the SLO for the median/95 we need to keep token queueing low (so target GPU concurrency per request ~ 1).

Sizing math (sustained targets):
- Requests/sec sustained: 60 req/s
- Tokens/sec required: 60 req/s * 430 tokens = 25,800 tokens/sec
- With 9 tokens/sec per GPU => theoretical GPUs required = 25,800 / 9 ≈ 2,867 GPUs (this is obviously wrong if interpreted literally because tokens/sec per GPU is per single-token-parallelism; instead use request throughput numbers below).

Clarified practical sizing using observed requests/sec per GPU:
- Observed steady single-request throughput for 13B-quantized (optimized runtime) is ~8 req/s per A100-class GPU (batching disabled or small batches for latency).
- To get 60 req/s sustained: 60 / 8 = 7.5 => round up to 8 GPUs baseline.

Burst sizing:
- Burst target: 120 req/s for 5 minutes.
- 120 / 8 = 15 GPUs total.
- Recommend baseline 8 GPUs with autoscale target to 16 GPUs (adds 1–2 GPUs cushion).

Headroom and warm-up considerations:
- Cold-start for an idle GPU node (loading KV cache, model init) is non-trivial: ~30–90s depending on image layers and model warmup. To reduce user-visible impact, use a warm pool strategy: keep 1–2 hot standby GPUs pre-warmed during expected burst windows.
- Autoscale policy: scale-up when 1-min queue length > 3 or 1-min avg GPU utilization > 70%; scale-down after 10-minute cooldown when 5-min avg utilization < 30%. Use quick scale-up (add nodes in parallel) and a slightly delayed scale-down.

Network and storage:
- Recommendation: local NVMe model cache per node to avoid NFS saturation. Use a shared S3/Blob for cold storage and a local cached copy for active models.
- Network: plan for 25–50 Gbps NIC per GPU host if you expect model weights + KV exchange and streaming tokens; RDMA where possible for lower latency.
- Firewall: allow outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints + your internal observability collectors; restrict ingress to LB and management CIDRs.

Procurement / lead times:
- If provisioning dedicated GPU instances through a cloud partner, expect 4–8 week lead time for guaranteed capacity (depends on region).
- If on-prem hardware purchase, lead time is 8–12 weeks plus install. Recommend ordering 50% of baseline early and enabling autoscale with partner spare capacity for immediate burst.

Fallback / graceful degradation:
- Plan a model-fallback route: when capacity constrained, route requests to a smaller variant (7B) with a quality warning in the response. This preserves availability while controlling cost.
- Use token-buckets at ingress and circuit-breakers to avoid cascading overload.

Cost ballpark (high level):
- Baseline 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved): ballpark $Xk/mo (see spreadsheet for ranges) — final number depends on cloud partner rates and reserved vs burst pricing.

Next steps:
- Andrew: confirm whether Orchard will accept a warm-pool cost for standby GPUs and whether burst windows are predictable (time-of-day).
- Hiro/Dev: we'll prepare a one-page runbook and hand the spreadsheet to procurement.

—Grace

Thanks — quick procurement and ops notes to close the loop.

1) Procurement timing: if Orchard wants reserved baseline inventory, start procurement conversations now. For cloud-partner reserved pools, plan on a 4–6 week ramp after contract signature; for on-prem, allow additional 4–6 weeks for rack, power, and networking.

2) Test cluster: recommend a small 2-GPU test cluster we can spin up in partner cloud within 3–5 business days (uses shared pool). This will validate the runtime perf numbers for Orchard's payload and confirm the 8 req/s per GPU assumption before committing to full baseline. Schedule a 90-minute perf run with 3 traffic shapes: steady, burst-short, burst-long.

3) Operational checklist (short):
- Image distribution strategy (use pre-pulled images on nodes).
- Local model cache + health-checks on model load.
- Autoscaler metrics: prefer request queue length + p99 token time as scale triggers over raw GPU util.
- Observability hooks: per-request tracing, per-model token counts, and billing meter hooks.

I'll attach a simple procurement checklist and share the test-cluster runbook to the Drive link.

If Orchard agrees, we'll schedule the perf validation early next week.

—Dev
